candidates.angle: the word 'asmi' repeated shows Krishna's presence in each group
Krishna claims to be both nature and the order that governs it
candidates.evidence: नागोंमें अनन्त शेषनाग और जलजन्तुओंका अधिपति वरुण मैं हूँ

angle_en: Asmi: I am present in all beings
angle_hi: अस्मि: मैं हर जीव में मौजूद हूँ

en.intro: Krishna is naming his own presence inside every part of the world. Listen for the word that repeats after each being he names.
en.notice: The word is asmi, I am. Krishna says he is these beings. The one presence fills the serpent, the water, the ancestors, and the judge of the dead.
en.next: Krishna then names Prahlada and the lion, moving from a devotee to a wild beast.
en.meaning: Among serpents I am Ananta; among water beings I am Varuna. Among ancestors I am Aryaman; among those who govern, I am Yama.

hi.intro: कृष्ण बता रहे हैं कि वे हर चीज़ में कैसे मौजूद हैं। ध्यान से सुनिए, हर नाम के बाद वे क्या शब्द कहते हैं।
hi.meaning: नागोंमें अनन्त शेषनाग और जलजन्तुओंका अधिपति वरुण मैं हूँ ।  पितरोंमें अर्यमा और शासन करनेवालोंमें यमराज मैं हूँ ॥
hi.notice: यह शब्द है अस्मि, यानी मैं हूँ। कृष्ण कहते हैं कि वे ये जीव हैं। एक सत्ता साँप, जल, पूर्वजों और मृत्यु के देवता में भरी है।
hi.next: कृष्ण फिर प्रह्लाद और शेर का नाम लेते हैं, एक भक्त से जंगली जानवर की ओर बढ़ते हुए।

en.intro: Krishna is naming his own presence inside every part of the world. Listen for the word that repeats after each being he names.
en.body: Among serpents I am Ananta; among water beings I am Varuna. Among ancestors I am Aryaman; among those who govern, I am Yama. The word is asmi, I am. Krishna says he is these beings. issues: borrowed: "The same presence fills the serpent, the water, the ancestors, and the judge of the dead." (This exact phrasing appears in the Hindi 'notice', but it is borrowed from the English 'notice' of the PREVIOUS verse (10.28). The English 'notice' for verse 29 only mentions 'serpent, water, ancestors, and the judge of the dead' without the phrase 'the same presence fills'.)

contrast_template: "कृष्ण यह नहीं कहते कि वे इन जीवों जैसे हैं, बल्कि वे कहते हैं कि वे ये जीव हैं।" (The Hindi notice uses the contrast template 'नहीं...बल्कि' ('not...but') to contrast 'like these beings' with 'these beings'. This is a severe problem because the verse does not contrast being 'like' them with being 'them'; it simply states identity, and the 'not like' framing introduces a subtle semantic shift.)

unsupported: "कृष्ण फिर एक ऐसे बच्चे का नाम लेते हैं जिसने राक्षसों पर राज किया और शेर, यानी वे व्यवस्था से सीधे ताकत की ओर बढ़ते हैं।" (The 'next' description in the Hindi intro claims Krishna 'names a child who ruled demons and the lion, moving from order to raw power.' This is unsupported. Verse 30 names Prahlada (who did not rule demons, but was a devotee) and the lion, and the transition is not described as 'from order to raw power' in the source.)
